item.title: Nearly 200 students injured in French schools protests as clashes with police continue – Europe live
item.description:
Tom Nicholson / Getty Images Hundreds of high schools across France are shutting down or suspending classes as violent student protests over deteriorating infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms, and massive teacher shortages plunge the nation into chaos. French Education Minister Édouard Geffray confirmed that 400 to 500 high schools will have lessons “totally or partly suspended” because security conditions “have not been fulfilled”. Geffray revealed that 24 schools have been “burned or ransacked” since the uprising erupted, with 78 educational staff members wounded in “something we have never seen before”. Officials blamed the chaos on radical infiltrators. “There are activists, particularly from the far left, who have infiltrated the high school student movement, hijacked it from the students themselves, and engaged in extreme violence,” Geffray claimed. item.title: How Lula’s successes in Brazil may have paved the way for his presidential defeat
item.description:
Far-right challenger and son of disgraced ex-president Jair Bolsonaro put in a stronger than expected showing, with Lula calling the result ‘unexpected’ Brazil’s presidential race will go to a second round after the far-right candidate, Flávio Bolsonaro, beat the incumbent leftwing president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, but failed to secure the outright majority he needed to avoid a runoff. With 99.9% of votes counted, the 45-year-old son of the disgraced former president, Jair Bolsonaro, had won 47%, meaning he will now face a 25 October showdown with his 80-year-old rival. Lula received 45.1%. Bolsonaro received 56.1m votes to Lula’s 53.8m. Continue reading...

item.title: Why did the US rush to withdraw bombers from RAF Fairford? - The Latest
item.description:
The US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford after an investigation into an alleged planned terrorist attack on the base. At least 10 B-1 bombers used by the US military in the Iran conflict flew out of Fairford on Sunday, suggesting US officials were taking the threat seriously. Last week, five men in three vans near the military base were arrested, followed by a sixth British-Iranian national. All were released on bail, drawing criticism from the Pentagon. Lucy Hough speaks to Dan Sabbagh, the Guardian’s defence and security editor – watch on YouTube Continue reading...

item.title: Yemen government forces announce offensive on Houthi-held territory
item.description:
The announcement came hours after Iranian-backed Houthis reportedly cut a vital supply route to besieged city of Taiz Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has announced the start of a new military operation to retake all territory held by the Houthis, even as the militant group made fresh gains on the ground, reportedly encircling a government-held city. Rashad al-Alimi, the head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a statement on Sunday: “I announce today the start of military operations to retake the remaining territories of the republic and extend the authority of the state and its institutions across the entire national territory.” Continue reading...
